$comment: DERIVED, not verbatim. Written by this library from the prose of RFC 9162. Source .cache/rfc-9162.txt (RFC 9162, Certificate Transparency Version 2.0, sha256 a0e432ce7580c99fcc8faf0cf3f6191f9ce6b4864f949158e020d4ecb295081f). RFC 9162 Section 5 gives these messages in prose and ships no JSON Schema. INSTANCE: the 2xx JSON response of get-all-by-hash (Section 5.5). Table 5 lists three cases whose responses are unioned, and none may be true, in which case the front end MUST return an empty response: so no member is required and {} is valid (an empty JSON object is the reading of 'empty response' taken here: inferred). A consistency proof accompanies the latest STH (Table 5, case 2), so consistency without sth is rejected (inferred). Instances are JSON values as received; binary fields stay base64 text and are not decoded (RFC 4648 Section 4, per Section 5). A pattern ^AQ[...] on a TransItem field binds the first two decoded octets, the VersionedTransType code of Section 4.5, because base64 of 0x01 0x0T begins AQ (every code here has 0 in its high nibble) and the low nibble T confines the third character to a block of four, its other two bits coming from the next octet; hence four characters per code in each pattern. The pattern states what a v2 log emits; it is not a client acceptance test, since a v2 client MUST NOT construe a non-v2 SCT (rfc-9162#R-0069) or an unrecognized TransItem type (rfc-9162#R-0079) as an error. Fields the RFC does not define are allowed (Section 5: any fields not understood SHOULD be ignored). A constraint marked inferred is a reading this library made, not a statement of the source. This schema cannot check the TransItem body, signatures, or any cross-field relation: those are in ../messages.yaml (constrained_by and notes per field).
